name: Whey protein
short: Reviews link chronic, excessive use to possible kidney and liver effects (called unsubstantiated in a published comment), and whey to acne; a 6-month randomised trial found acne no worse than control.
text: A systematic review of 11 experimental and randomised studies found that most associated harm with chronic and abusive use of whey protein, with the kidneys and liver the main organs affected, and that other studies related whey protein to aggression, acne and changes in the gut microbiota; a published comment on that review described the claims of adverse effects on human kidney and liver function as unsubstantiated. A narrative review of 21 preclinical and human studies reported both beneficial and detrimental outcomes and suggested caution with protein intake in people with compromised liver or kidney function and in those susceptible to acne. In a 6-month double-blind randomised trial in 49 men with mild to moderate acne, 30 g of whey protein daily was non-inferior to a non-whey supplement for changes in acne lesion counts and severity. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
